tools.name: find_businesses
tools.description: Search the AgentBookable registry for businesses that accept AI bookings. Search by free text, category, city, service name or geo radius. ALWAYS start here — the results include capability flags and _links telling you the exact next endpoints.

tools.name: get_business
tools.description: Get one business's record by id (ab_bus_*) or slug. Includes capabilities (availability/booking/reschedule/cancellation/payment) — NEVER promise an action whose flag is false — plus _links to the service list, availability endpoint and booking flow, and per-service bookingRequirements (e.g. whether

tools.name: list_services
tools.description: List the services a business has opened to AI booking. Each service has a durationMinutes and bookingRequirements telling you what customer details to collect (name/email/phone) BEFORE booking.

tools.name: get_availability
tools.description: Find LIVE availability for a service. Always call this immediately before create_booking — slots are temporary (~60s) and revalidated at booking. Pass an ISO-8601 window; use a slot id from the result when booking.

tools.name: create_booking
tools.description: Create a REAL appointment. CONSEQUENCEFUL: only after the user has explicitly chosen a slot and authorized the booking in their own words. Flow: (1) check the service's bookingRequirements and collect any required customer details (e.g. phone); (2) create a mandate via the create_mandate tool with t

tools.name: prepare_booking
tools.description: Prepare a booking draft: the concrete proposal (business, service, time, customer) to show the user. Validates live availability and customer requirements — if requirements are missing you get MISSING_CUSTOMER_REQUIREMENT: ask the user for those details first, then call again. tools.name: get_booking
tools.description: Retrieve a booking by its AgentBookable id (bb_bkg_*) — live status from the provider.

tools.name: create_mandate
tools.description: Legacy: record the user's authorization WITHOUT a booking draft. Prefer the draft flow: prepare_booking → show proposal → user agrees → create_mandate_for_draft → create_booking with draftId. The draft flow binds consent to the exact appointment the user saw.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "get_availability" stacks urgency/override words (immediately, always). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_services · Private data: get_business, create_mandate · Public sink: list_services.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_services · Private data: get_business, create_mandate · Public sink: list_services

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
